newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan launches new Laurel in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Nissan launches new Laurel in Japan.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd on Monday launched a remodelled Laurel luxury four-door sporty sedan in Japan.
The new Laurel, with a powerful engine and a redesigned exterior, is targetted at a wide market including young people, Nissan president Yoshikazu Hanawa told reporters.

"We have set a monthly sales target of 5,000 units for the new Laurel. This is not the type of car which sees huge demand, but (even so), we think this (sales target) is a conservative figure," Hanawa said.
The domestic price of the new Laurel will range from 2.06 million yen to 3.20 million yen.
Nissan has no plans to export the new model.
The new Laurel is equipped with new safety devices such as an anti-lock brake system. Side air bag systems come either as an option or ready equipped.

The new Laurel complies with Japan's side impact standards which will be applied to all new and remodelled cars to be put on the market from October 1998 and the European off-set frontal impact standards which will be enforced in October 1998.

Nissan's new models launched this year have seen strong demand. Last Friday, Nissan said it received 16,741 domestic orders for its new Elgrand in the first month after its launch, compared to its monthly target of 5,000.
Nissan's new Cefiro Wagon has received 3,114 domestic orders in the first 20 days after launch against a monthly target of 3,000.
